eu-tiktok-dsa.name: European Commission preliminary findings on TikTok's addictive design
eu-tiktok-dsa.outcome: Published February 6, 2026: Commission found infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications and recommender breach the Digital Services Act; suggested disabling infinite scroll over time and screen time breaks, including during the night
eu-tiktok-dsa.limits: Preliminary findings only; TikTok can reply and the outcome is not decided.
eu-tiktok-dsa.locator: "needs to change the basic design of its service"

ny-safe-kids.name: New York SAFE for Kids Act final rules
ny-safe-kids.outcome: Under-18s default to chronological feeds of accounts they follow; no notifications midnight to 6am without parental consent; effective January 25, 2027
ny-safe-kids.limits: Not yet in effect; applies only to minors; relies on age checks that raise privacy questions.
ny-safe-kids.locator: "civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation"

australia-under16.name: Australia social media minimum age
australia-under16.outcome: From Dec 10, 2025, ten platforms must take reasonable steps to stop under-16s holding accounts; fines up to about A$49.5 million
australia-under16.limits: Contested; age limits have been easy to get around; outcomes not yet measured.
australia-under16.locator: Penalties section: 150,000 penalty units for a body corporate

minnesota-warning.name: Minnesota social media mental health warning law
minnesota-warning.outcome: From July 1, 2026, platforms must show a warning with the 988 lifeline each time the app opens
minnesota-warning.limits: New; no evidence yet on whether warnings change use; tech companies have been reported to challenge it.
minnesota-warning.locator: "cannot be removed until the user either acknowledges it or leaves"

states-v-meta.name: Multistate lawsuit against Meta over youth features
states-v-meta.place: 41 US states and the District of Columbia (Washington, DC)
states-v-meta.outcome: Attorneys general sued Meta in federal court alleging features built to drive compulsive use by young people; the article says Meta depends on holding young users' attention on Facebook and Instagram, and the suit calls out Instagram features like likes, filters and recommendations
states-v-meta.limits: Allegations in a lawsuit, not findings; case ongoing at time of source.
states-v-meta.locator: "cultivating addiction to boost corporate profits" (California AG Bonta)

ncsl-tracker.name: National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) tracker of 2025 state social media and children bills
ncsl-tracker.outcome: Over 45 states and Puerto Rico introduced 300+ bills in 2025; at least 20 states enacted laws, including school phone limits
ncsl-tracker.limits: Counts as of Oct 24, 2025; a tracker, not an outcome study.
ncsl-tracker.locator: "Over 45 states and Puerto Rico introduced over 300 bills"

dutch-nijmegen.name: Radboud University study of school phone ban in two Nijmegen schools
dutch-nijmegen.outcome: Teachers saw more attention in class and more conversation; online bullying fell; pupil approval dropped from 6.8 to 4.8 out of 10
dutch-nijmegen.limits: Two schools; grades effect unknown; pupils missed school apps and contact with parents.
dutch-nijmegen.locator: Headline: school ban on phones results in concentration and conversation

dutch-national.name: Dutch government survey of 317 high schools after national phone ban
dutch-national.outcome: Three-quarters of schools reported better concentration; two-thirds better social climate
dutch-national.limits: School self-reports, not test scores; page blocked, seen only in search summaries.

one-sec-pnas.name: one sec self-nudge app field study (PNAS)
one-sec-pnas.outcome: 280 users over six weeks; 36% of attempts to open target app ended in closing it; actual openings fell 57%
one-sec-pnas.limits: Users chose the app themselves, so self-selection bias; co-authored by the app's founder.
one-sec-pnas.locator: "decreased users' actual opening of target apps by 57%"

grayscale-uc.name: Grayscale screen study, Alex Holte (UC Blue Ash)
grayscale-uc.outcome: About 220 students who set phones to grayscale cut use by an average of 39 minutes a day. Alex J. Holte is an assistant professor of psychology at UC Blue Ash College, University of Cincinnati
grayscale-uc.limits: College students; short studies; anxiety effects small.
grayscale-uc.locator: "reduction of smartphone use by an average of 39 minutes per day"

abcd-bedroom.name: ABCD study: phones out of the bedroom and teen sleep (Nagata, UCSF)
abcd-bedroom.outcome: Among ~9,400 11–12-year-olds, phones kept out of the bedroom were linked to longer, better sleep, and a follow-up a year later found this persisted; silenced phones did worse than phones turned off. Led by Dr. Jason Nagata, associate professor of pediatrics at the University of California, San Francisco
abcd-bedroom.limits: Observational, in young teens; association not proof. Nagata says the advice goes for grownups too, but adults were not studied.
abcd-bedroom.locator: "may still be woken up overnight by vibrations or lights"

facebook-deactivation.name: Facebook deactivation experiment (Allcott, Gentzkow and colleagues)
facebook-deactivation.outcome: Paid users who left Facebook for four weeks gained about an hour a day, spent more time with friends and family, and reported small gains in happiness; several weeks after, reported use of the Facebook mobile app was about 11 minutes (22 percent) lower than in the control group
facebook-deactivation.limits: Four weeks before an election; paid participants; effects small.
facebook-deactivation.locator: "small but significant increases in self-reported individual life satisfaction"

android-bedtime.name: Android Digital Wellbeing Bedtime mode and app timers
android-bedtime.outcome: Bedtime mode can turn the screen black and white on a schedule or when charging at night; app timers close an app after a daily limit
android-bedtime.limits: Menus differ by phone maker; limits are easy to override.
android-bedtime.locator: "Changes your screen to black and white"

apple-screen-time.name: Apple Screen Time schedules and time allowances
apple-screen-time.outcome: Screen Time lets you limit app categories like social media by daily time and by schedule
apple-screen-time.limits: Page opened describes the family version; limits you set for yourself can be dismissed.

instagram-sleep-mode.name: Instagram Teen Accounts sleep mode
instagram-sleep-mode.outcome: Teen accounts mute notifications and auto-reply to messages from 10pm to 7am every day
instagram-sleep-mode.limits: Teen accounts only; 16 and 17 year olds can change some settings.
instagram-sleep-mode.locator: "sleep mode turned on from 10 PM to 7 AM every day"

light-phone-3.name: Light Phone III
light-phone-3.outcome: Minimalist phone with calls, messages, maps, music and alarm but no social media or browser; $799
light-phone-3.limits: Expensive; some features missing; many people still need a smartphone for work or banking.

brick-device.name: Brick NFC app blocker
brick-device.outcome: Tap the phone on a small block to lock up to 50 chosen apps; tap again to unlock; five emergency unlocks
brick-device.limits: Costs money (about $59 US); you can still leave the block nearby.
brick-device.locator: "Brick is a small grey square with its logo on top"

wait-until-8th.name: Wait Until 8th pledge
wait-until-8th.outcome: Parents pledge to delay smartphones to the end of 8th grade; activates when 10 families in a grade sign; 155,000+ parents signed
wait-until-8th.limits: Self-reported counts; delays a smartphone, not all screens.
wait-until-8th.locator: Pledge activates when 10 families from the same grade and school sign

smartphone-free-childhood.name: Smartphone Free Childhood parent pact
smartphone-free-childhood.outcome: Launched in the UK in early 2024 by parents; over 140,000 parents from 13,500 schools pledged to delay smartphones until 14
smartphone-free-childhood.limits: Counts reported by a local council (Brighton and Hove) from the campaign; page doesn't say how it started beyond parents in the UK; outcomes not studied.
smartphone-free-childhood.locator: "over 140,000 parents from 13,500 schools have signed a pact"

five-calls.name: 5 Calls
five-calls.outcome: Free site and app that gives scripts for calling your members of Congress on an issue
five-calls.limits: Federal focus; most addictive-design bills are at the state level.
five-calls.locator: Pick an issue from the list, then call your congressperson
